thread:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] HIGH SEV: GPU OOM on gpu-node-17 despite reported headroom ~1.1GB. Container inference-runtime-prod-7f8f crashed; automatic spare allocation retried and failed. Triggered at 2187659999. Monitoring link: https://console.redwood/alerts/2187659999

maria: oncall - ack. seeing a flurry of OOMs across the node pool?

aj: I can see 2 pods on node-17 in CrashLoopBackOff, one evicted. Noting 'allocated reserved blocks mismatch' in kubelet logs.

sanket: quick question — were we doing any large prefetches or batch warmup on that cluster? Trying to reason why headroom vs OOM.

kevin: yes, there was a background cold-start prefetch job ramping yesterday for a new quantized variant. Might have grabbed KV cache reservations.

maria: ok, start triage. Priority: 1) mitigate customer impact 2) gather logs 3) avoid noisy restarts.

ops-bot: automatic mitigation attempted: drained node-17, cordon succeeded, attempted pod reschedule -> 2 failures, action logged.

tara: paste of kube + nvidia-smi from node-17:
```bash
$ kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-17 --selector=app=inference-runtime
NAME                                      READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
inference-runtime-7f8f                    0/1     CrashLoopBackOff    5          3h   gpu-node-17
inference-runtime-9c1b                    0/1     Evicted             1          2h   gpu-node-17

$ ssh root@gpu-node-17 sudo nvidia-smi -q | egrep -A5 "FB Memory Usage"
FB Memory Usage
    Total                       : 24576 MiB
    Used                        : 23324 MiB
    Free                        : 1252 MiB

$ dmesg | tail -n 30 | egrep -i "oom|cuda|nvlink|reservation"
[..] CUDA: failed to allocate 2147483648 bytes: out of memory
[..] allocator: reserved blocks count mismatch: expected 12 got 4
```

aj: interesting — node reports ~1.2GB free, but processes still OOM when trying to allocate 2GB contiguous. Looks like fragmentation and pinned reserves are preventing allocation.

lucy: we've seen fragmentation when prefix KV caches pin many small blocks, leaving no contiguous region for larger allocations. Could be the prefetch job + several live sessions with long KV caches.

sanket: suggested immediate mitigations: 1) reduce prefetch concurrency 2) kill highest-memory pods gracefully to free contiguous chunks 3) enable fallback to smaller model variant for traffic to that pool.

maria: do not mass kill without assessing customer impact. Which customers routed through gpu-node-17?

kevin: routing table shows three tenants with sticky sessions: ai-corp-prod (35% qps), beta-chat (15%), internal-evals (5%). Remaining traffic on that node was ~55 RPS.

tara: we can forcibly migrate ai-corp-prod to dedicated fallback pool (model: redwood-medium-quant) and reduce concurrency to 1. That should shave peak allocation by ~40%.

aj: I'll perform a controlled scale command to move traffic and restart a single failing pod for fast recovery. Plan:
1) scale down prefetch job: `kubectl scale job/prefetch-warmup --replicas=0`
2) update service route for ai-corp-prod to fallback pool: `rbacctl route update ai-corp-prod --pool=fallback-medium`
3) restart one pod on node-17: `kubectl delete pod inference-runtime-7f8f` (allow reschedule to another node)

maria: go for 1 and 2. Hold on 3 until we confirm traffic has moved. Inform customers.

aj: prefetch job scaled to 0 (done). Routing updated for ai-corp-prod -> fallback-medium (done). Still seeing high pinned memory from two remaining pods.

ops-bot: customer-notify-bot queued messages to ai-corp-prod and beta-chat: "We are experiencing GPU allocation instability; traffic will be routed to fallback model for degraded perf. ETA to full recovery: 30-60m."

lucy: recommendation: flush KV cache for long-running sessions instead of killing pods. We have an admin endpoint: `POST /admin/kv/flush?session=<id>` but need session ids. Can we target the top memory sessions?

aj: collecting top memory handles from runtime metrics... returning top-3 sessions by vram: s-9841 (3.2GB pinned), s-6712 (2.4GB), s-1203 (1.6GB). Proposing to flush s-9841 and s-6712 first.

maria: do it. Coordinate with the eng team owning those sessions (tag: @kenny). If flush fails, we escalate to restart the pod.

aj: flush commands issued for s-9841 and s-6712 — responses: OK for s-6712, s-9841 timed out (session unresponsive).

aj: because s-9841 is unresponsive and holding a large pinned block, I'm going to cordon node-17 and restart the one CrashLoopBackOff pod to free allocations. Will do graceful delete to let rescheduler place elsewhere.

maria: acknowledged. Proceed. Remember to set maintenance annotation so the autoscaler doesn't fill node-17 immediately.

aj: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17` -> done. `kubectl annotate node gpu-node-17 maintenance=true` -> done. Deleting pod inference-runtime-7f8f now.

ops-bot: Pod deletion in progress. Scheduler placing pod on gpu-node-22.

aj: new pod landed on gpu-node-22 and is Ready. Memory usage on node-17 dropped and free contiguous region increased to ~3.6GB. Crash frequency stopped.

tara: great. Now we need to do the postmortem checklist:
- capture allocator and slab debug logs
- capture reservation bookkeeping snapshots
- reproduce with a prefetch workload in staging
- evaluate changes to default prefetch concurrency and reserved-block sizing

maria: customer impact summary: ai-corp-prod experienced degraded latency and fallback model for ~12 minutes. beta-chat saw ~5% error spike while sessions migrated. No data loss reported.

kevin: triage notes: root cause appears to be fragmentation + pinned KV reservations caused by long-lived prefetch + one unresponsive session holding a large contiguous reservation. Node headroom reporting (free memory) was accurate but non-contiguous. The allocator couldn't satisfy large contiguous allocation request -> CUDA OOM.

lucy: mitigation proposals (short-term):
- default prefetch concurrency -> 1 for production pools with >75% utilization
- expose KV flush as operator action and add autoscale step to flush oldest sessions when contiguous free < X GB
- monitor contiguous free (not just total free) in node health dashboards

aj: assigning follow-ups:
- sanket: add contiguous-free metric to node exporter (P1, 48h)
- tara: add graceful admin KV flush endpoint to our runbook and automation (P1, 72h)
- kevin: change prefetch job config to cap concurrency and add config flag for reserved-blocks (P2, next deploy)
- lucy: create a repro in staging with prefetch + large-session pattern (P2)

maria: handing off to aj for the remainder of the oncall window. I'm stepping out in 25m but will be available via DM for escalation.

aj: taking handoff. I'll run the follow-ups and keep watch for any reoccurrence. If the node behaves, we'll uncordon after 2h and remove maintenance annotation.

incidents-bot: Incident marked stable at 2187662450. Postmortem required. Severity: P2 (customer impact limited, recovery via reroute).
